I’ve also had a very painful pregnancy this time around. I don’t remember at what week my doctor diagnosed me with vulvar varicosities. Then later with anemia to contribute to the discomforts. Despite trying Physio therapy, chiropractor, massage, baths, vulvar compression garment, belly band, I’m still in pain. Baths have been the most relief I’ve been able to find but it’s very short lived. I’m up to 2-3 baths a day and a lot of intermittent side lying breaks. Unfortunately, they’re right, you’re going to get heavier and more uncomfortable. I don’t have any answers but you’ll probably have to trial and error what works best for you. Also, some days different things bring me more relief than they did the day before. Best of luck.

I can assure you that the uppababy stroller will almost certainly be miles better than a random Amazon brand. They cost as much as they do for a reason, you get what you pay for. 

For my first kid I had a very middle of the road Chicco bravo stroller that cost about $250. It was compatible with our infant seat and then we used it as a regular stroller. It was a perfectly fine stroller and I had no major complaints. 

For the second kid we splurged on an uppababy vista to have a double stroller. It is SO much nicer. The wheels and suspension are better so while the bravo struggled on anything that wasn’t regular pavement (like grass) the vista handles it no problem. The bravo was challenging to push with one hand (like if I was carrying a hot beverage in the other hand) and would make my forearm ache after a bit. I can quite literally push/ steer the vista with one finger. The basket underneath holds a truly incredible amount of stuff. When I quit my job I moved my whole office out in the bottom of that stroller. The sun shade is huge and can almost fully cover baby. My biggest complaint is that there’s no built in parent tray/ cup holder - for a thousand dollar stroller they could have included that. But I got a momcozy one to add. It’s also heavy but I don’t have to lift it very often. 

I promise you that if you describe yourself as an avid walker, you want to invest in a good stroller. It doesn’t have to be an uppababy and it doesn’t have to be brand new, but I’d steer you away from Amazon brands.

title: KT Tape & stretch marks warning
text:
Hi all - I am really bummed I did this to myself but here we are. 

Please keep in mind that I do not have stretch mark prone skin. I didn’t get one single mark on my skin with my first baby.  

However, during this second pregnancy I have been seeing pregnant people using KT tape to tape up their belly for support. So I decided to try it. Watched a YouTube video for instructions and got to it. 

Everything was fine but I felt like the tape was burning me. I was itchy and felt really off wherever the tape was. So I got in the shower to take it off bc the adhesive was so tight on my skin I couldn’t peel it off. My whole belly was itchy at this point. 

I peeled off the wet tape and washed off the remaining adhesive, noticing that there were red marks, wherever I pulled the tape off. It also seems like I had red marks around where the tape was on the bottom of my belly. Sometimes I get allergic reactions to Band-Aids so I was thinking I must have been having an allergic reaction to the adhesive in the KT tape.

Now here I am about four days later and the entire bottom half of my belly (where most of the tape was) is covered in deep red itchy stretch marks. It looks hideous and I’m really hoping it goes away. But something tells me I am going to have this forever now. Like I must have done physical damage to my skin, as if it were stretched to the max and I stretched it more than it could handle by using the KT tape. I am so so so mad at myself!

title: Pelvic Girdle Pain + Exercise??
text:
I’m a 31F 30 weeks pregnant and have been pretty active throughout my pregnancy. I’ve continued to Climb top rope, although have slowed down on that quite a bit. I weight train, go to yoga, and walk. At 26 weeks I went backpacking 4 days around 18 miles and felt great! Since my second trimester I have some pelvic and groin pain especially after walking. I would make sure to rest and the pain would go away after 1-2 days. Because of that I use a belly band anytime I’m going to be walking for longer than 10 minutes.   
The past week I was on vacation with my husband’s family. We went for a 3 mile walk one day, another day I was in a SUP and played “soccer” with our 4yo nephew. And lastly we took the canoes out for a half day trip about 6 hours down a river and back. After the canoe ride was exhausted the entire day. It took so long for me to recover. I didn’t even paddle 1/3 of the way because I was so tired. My husband paddled us both back. Since then, my pelvic and groin pain has not gone away :( I researched my symptoms and this lead me to pelvic girdle pain (PGP). Apparently it’s pretty common. And it makes sense. Initially my thoughts were that this is all part of pregnancy and I just really need to slow down now that I’m in my 3rd trimester and growing a lot. But I love being active and I’m not sure what is safe and what might aggravate the pain. I’ve found some helpful links online that suggest not to sit for longer than 30 minutes, take smaller steps while walking, sit to out pants on, etc etc.   
Anyone who has been able to stay active despite some pain? Online it’s also said not to lift anything heavy? Does this mean I can’t weight train? I’m thinking I’ll have to sit down to left weights? So no more squats??   
Going to ask for a PT referral at my next prenatal appt but tbh don’t have much faith that I’ll get a good referral through my HMO.  
OH I also heard that having PGP can lead to a more painful birth?!?!!!!   
Any thoughts, advice, experiences would be greatly appreciated.

Braxton hicks feel more like intense tightness around your stomach like a band, sometimes a bit painful. If your belly is sticking out in specific places at these times, it’ll be likely baby moving and trying to get snug. It’s getting a little cramped for them at this stage as they get so big, and want to move around a lot. A good way to tell is to poke all round your belly gently and it will feel like a solid rock when it’s braxton hicks, and not just in one place. For my first pregnancy I didn’t get braxton hicks until 34 weeks along and I knew straight away it was that, despite thinking several other things were braxton hicks before it. It’s a very distinct feeling
